newsitem.title: ITALY: Suspected Naples crime boss arrested.
newsitem.headline: Suspected Naples crime boss arrested.

text.p: Italian police said on Friday they had arrested Marzio Sepe, suspected head of the Naples-based Camorra crime syndicate who is accused of complicity in dozens of murders.
Police said agents from the DIA anti-Mafia police force surprised Marzio Sepe as he waited to meet someone outside an abandoned cottage east of Naples on Thursday night.
Sepe, 42, who had been a fugitive for four years, tried to run away but was captured, they said.
Police said Sepe was wanted on 15 arrest warrants for charges ranging from Mafia association to extortion and murder and had recently been sentenced in his absence to life in prison for murder.
Investigators said they believed Sepe succeeded Carmine Alfieri as boss of the Camorra following Alfieri's arrest in September 1992.
They said Alfieri, who began giving state's evidence after his arrest, and other Camorra turncoats had told them that Sepe took part in, or helped plan, dozens of murders.
The turncoats also have said Sepe had been in charge of collecting bribes from construction companies to win public works contracts, investigators said.
They said Sepe was being held in a jail in the Naples area and would be interviewed in the next few days by magistrates.
